content:
Simplify the geometric sum:
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k = \frac{-1+(-1)^n}{2}.
\]
For the alternating arithmetic part:
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k k =
\begin{cases}
\frac n2, & n \text{ even},\\[4pt]
-\frac{n+1}{2}, & n \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus
\[
S_n = 3\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k k - 2\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k.
\]

For odd \(n\):
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k = -1,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k k = -\frac{n+1}{2}.
\]
So
\[
S_n = 3\left(-\frac{n+1}{2}\right) - 2(-1)
= \frac{1-3n}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
S_{11} = \frac{1-33}{2} = -16.
\]

For even \(n\):
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k = 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^n (-1)^k k = \frac n2.
\]
So
\[
S_n = 3\cdot \frac n2 = \frac{3n}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
S_{20} = \frac{3\cdot 20}{2} = 30.
\]

Therefore,
\[
S_{11}+S_{20} = -16+30=14.
\]

\[
\boxed{14}
\]
